clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death and your move into secondary school, 1987–1994
clusters.reason: Around the time you began secondary in 1987, you joined the chess squad out of your depth and felt unsettled; your grandfather died in June 1991 as you left home for the conservatory that autumn. Your wrist injury stopped your playing within weeks, you lost your footing with Rafe and drifted through the community college with late nights and low mood; your father came back into the family after years away in 1989 while your stepfather's marriage to your mother was shaken. Your mother saw you filling in your college forms rather than doing it yourself, and you leaned hard on Rafe as you both struggled. The exchange to Lisbon in January 1994 and your regained drive sit where the period settles, though your anxiety about your father's notice of you persisted. Each shift piles close to another across these years, with no long quiet between them.

clusters.name: Your relationship with Marisol ending and your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From autumn 2001, you ran out of steam for performing and your anxiety climbed; your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 as your audition fell apart that January and you began casting about for what came next. You left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in September 2002 distant from family and friends, met Marisol at a winter party, moved to Fenwick with her in June 2003, and split with her within months. You sank into deep depression once you were back in Thornbury, could not face your family, and relied on friends instead; your mother pushed to visit you at Alder Creek that July and you kept the door shut on her. You left for nursing school in August 2008 and stopped speaking to your mother; your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home and died in February 2004, where you visited her hung over on the way to the airport. Your functioning fell and your relationship to your family narrowed as your own trouble deepened, shifts piling close around the loss of both the relationship and the person who mattered.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her mother's retirement party, 2019
clusters.reason: Around your wedding in March 2017, you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; in October 2019, Wren's mother retired and the family gathered at the lake house. Wren was swamped with a street party, a fundraising dinner and the drive to the lake, her symptom and anxiety climbing as her functioning fell; you moved into overfunctioning to settle her with a strict plan. Wren's family talks all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear; you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and felt you don't belong, pulling back as the others rose. Wren grew anxious when you had no sleep at family occasions, long quiet drives home afterward. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, and your sister's first grandchild to the family was due that autumn. The shifts in these weeks are yours and Wren's; no one else's show in those months, but the period holds together around your move into Wren's family and the strain it brings to your sleep and your distance from her when her own family gathers.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
